I have a yellow monopoly on Atlantic, Ventnor, and Marvin Gardens. I am cash-rich at $701. Player three has a light blue monopoly with hotels on Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut. That is a major rent threat.

I just passed through the light blue hotels on my way to Baltic Avenue and paid only $4 rent. I survived the gauntlet. I am now on Baltic Avenue.

I am now mapping the board to identify upcoming spaces after Baltic Avenue.

I mapped the full board sequence. From Baltic, rolling a 2 lands on Income Tax for $200. Rolling a 3 lands on Reading Railroad, where player one owns three railroads and charges $100.

Rolling a 4 from Baltic lands on Oriental Hotel for $550. Rolling a 6 lands on Vermont Hotel for $550. Rolling a 7 lands on Connecticut Hotel for $600. The combined probability of hitting any light blue hotel is roughly 39%. I can afford one hotel hit with my current cash without building.

Building three houses on the yellow monopoly would cost $1,350. That is far beyond my current cash of $701. The rent cliff at three houses yields roughly $800 to $850 per property. I cannot afford to build without risking bankruptcy.

Even one house on each yellow property costs $450, leaving only $251. That is still too little to survive a $550 hotel hit. Selling houses back would recover only about $75 each, so the shortfall remains. Mortgaging the monopoly requires selling all houses first, making any building attempt suicidal. The safer path is to keep all cash and mortgage Park Place for $175 if needed.

I have not actually cleared the light blue danger yet. My next roll from Baltic still carries a 39% chance of hitting a hotel. Building houses remains too risky. I am now considering whether to trade with other players.

No other player has enough cash to fund a safe three-house build on the yellow monopoly. Player one has $613, player two has $524, and player three has $591. None can cover the roughly $1,250 needed.

Trading Park Place for Boardwalk would be disastrous. Player two already owns Boardwalk and would complete the dark blue monopoly, giving them the strongest set on the board.

Player two cannot immediately hotel the dark blue set, but it remains a long-term win condition. Player one would only trade New York for an orange monopoly, which is irrelevant to my yellow strategy. Player three will not un-build their light blue hotels. Unowned properties are unavailable for purchase during this post-turn phase.

Mortgaging is unwise because it costs 10% interest and reduces income. Player two already paid $600 in rent from the light blue hotels, so player one may also hit them. Player one owns three railroads and two of three orange properties.

Player one would become extremely dangerous if they acquired New York, since the orange monopoly offers the best return on investment. My win condition is to develop the yellow monopoly safely. Park Place currently blocks player two from completing the dark blue set. The safest move is to end the turn and preserve cash. My buffer has improved slightly to $701, but building remains too risky.

I am now exploring a trade that would give me enough cash to safely build three houses on the yellow monopoly. Player two has only $524, but they want Park Place badly to complete the dark blue set. If I could acquire that cash plus another property, my total would rise to roughly $1,225. That would allow even building, since the rules require all properties in a monopoly to be built evenly.

I am now calculating the exact rent and cash implications of different house configurations on the yellow monopoly. A 3-3-2 build would cost $1,200 and leave only $25, which is too little to survive a hotel hit. A 2-2-2 build would cost $900 and leave $325, still short of the $600 buffer needed. A 1-1-1 build would cost $450 and leave $775, which survives a hotel hit but yields only about $130 in extra rent per property.

Player two can reach the yellow properties with doubles, but the probability is only about 5% to 8%. Even if they land there, undeveloped yellow rent is just $44 to $48, so building offers almost no return. Player three can also reach Atlantic and Ventnor from Pennsylvania Railroad with roughly an 8% chance. The expected rent from not building this round is negligible, so building does not pay off before the dangerous roll.

Player two could mortgage other properties to build dark blue houses, but that would make them lethal. Player three will not un-build their hotels. I am now considering trading with player one to block their orange monopoly or acquire railroads.

My win condition remains safe development of the yellow monopoly. The plan is to survive the next light-blue passage, accumulate cash from GO and rent, and only build houses once the combined cash and mortgage value can cover a hotel hit after construction.

I can survive the $600 hotel hit without mortgaging, leaving me with only $101 cash and $175 in mortgage. That is too little to build houses safely. If I avoid the hit, I keep my full $701 and continue accumulating. Player three's hotels could bankrupt other opponents, which would reduce competition but also enrich player three.

Player one can survive a $600 hotel hit with only $13 to $63 left, but mortgaging their three railroads would cripple them. Player two is already past the light blue set and will not threaten my yellow properties. Player three has hotels and can land on my yellow for just $44. No trade proposal looks worthwhile.

Mortgaging Park Place now would raise cash to $876. A 1-1-1 build costs $450 and leaves $426, which is still too low for a hotel hit of $600. Selling the three houses first would yield $651, enough to cover the hotel and leave $51. The yellow monopoly would remain unmortgaged but undeveloped.

I just passed through the light blue hotels on my way to Baltic Avenue and paid only $4 rent. I survived the gauntlet. I am now on Baltic Avenue.

I am now mapping the board to identify upcoming spaces after Baltic Avenue.

I mapped the full board sequence. From Baltic, rolling a 2 lands on Income Tax for $200. Rolling a 3 lands on Reading Railroad, where player one owns three railroads and charges $100.

Rolling a 4 from Baltic lands on Oriental Hotel for $550. Rolling a 6 lands on Vermont Hotel for $550. Rolling a 7 lands on Connecticut Hotel for $600. The combined probability of hitting any light blue hotel is roughly 39%. I can afford one hotel hit with my current cash without building.

Building three houses on the yellow monopoly would cost $1,350. That is far beyond my current cash of $701. The rent cliff at three houses yields roughly $800 to $850 per property. I cannot afford to build without risking bankruptcy.

Even one house on each yellow property costs $450, leaving only $251. That is still too little to survive a $550 hotel hit. Selling houses back would recover only about $75 each, so the shortfall remains. Mortgaging the monopoly requires selling all houses first, making any building attempt suicidal. The safer path is to keep all cash and mortgage Park Place for $175 if needed.

I have not actually cleared the light blue danger yet. My next roll from Baltic still carries a 39% chance of hitting a hotel. Building houses remains too risky. I am now considering whether to trade with other players.

No other player has enough cash to fund a safe three-house build on the yellow monopoly. Player one has $613, player two has $524, and player three has $591. None can cover the roughly $1,250 needed.

Trading Park Place for Boardwalk would be disastrous. Player two already owns Boardwalk and would complete the dark blue monopoly, giving them the strongest set on the board.

Player two cannot immediately hotel the dark blue set, but it remains a long-term win condition. Player one would only trade New York for an orange monopoly, which is irrelevant to my yellow strategy. Player three will not un-build their light blue hotels. Unowned properties are unavailable for purchase during this post-turn phase.

Mortgaging is unwise because it costs 10% interest and reduces income. Player two already paid $600 in rent from the light blue hotels, so player one may also hit them. Player one owns three railroads and two of three orange properties.

Player one would become extremely dangerous if they acquired New York, since the orange monopoly offers the best return on investment. My win condition is to develop the yellow monopoly safely. Park Place currently blocks player two from completing the dark blue set. The safest move is to end the turn and preserve cash. My buffer has improved slightly to $701, but building remains too risky.
